newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges Serbia to end domestic crisis quickly.
newsitem.headline: France urges Serbia to end domestic crisis quickly.

text.p: France on Saturday urged Serbian authorities to recognise opposition victories in November 17 municipal elections in Belgrade and 14 other towns quickly or risk creating permanent national divisions.
It also urged the authorities to do everything possible to avoid violent confrontations at Saturday's funeral for a man alleged to have been killed in rioting this week over the alleged vote fraud.

"The Serbian government must understand that the current differences between the authorities and the people could become permanent unless it quickly takes steps to calm the situation," the French Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"At stake are both national stability and the reintegration of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia into the international community," the ministry statement said.

France said its appeal was part of a joint campaign by the European Union and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to pressure Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to respect the OSCE recommendations.
A mission of the OSCE concluded this week that the Zajedno (Together) coalition had won Belgrade and 14 other towns in last month's poll, defeating the governing Socialist Party (SPS).

The Socialists' decision to ignore the opposition victories has led to nearly six weeks of street protests which have turned increasingy violent since Christmas eve when Zajedno activists fought rival socialist militants and riot police in Belgrade.
